result.verdict: promoted to tasks.json (priority 56). Single 18-line traverser change, no rebuild required.

hypothesis: Representing each inner node by multiple centroids (one per soft-cluster mode) instead of a single description embedding lets the traverser score a query against the closest mode, fixing misses where a category is semantically broad and its single centroid sits between two query distributions.

papers.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
papers.key_claim: Multi-vector representation captures finer-grained semantics than a single dense vector; max-pooling over vectors is the scoring rule.

papers.title: HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models
papers.key_claim: Soft assignment with temperature schedule produces per-node mixture distributions over children — already implemented in src/tool_index/scale/soft_cluster.py.

baseline.miss_breakdown: cat_391687b6 alone produces 11/27 misses; sibling clusters cat_c224869d and cat_246c3a14 are too close in embedding space

design.stage: Stage 4 (cluster_upward) — store M centroids per node instead of 1
design.centroids: M = min(K, ceil(sqrt(num_children))); compute via existing soft_cluster.py modes or k-means on child embeddings.
design.scoring: node_score(query) = max(cosine(query, c_i) for c_i in node.centroids) — ColBERT MaxSim restricted to inner nodes.
files_to_touch: src/tool_index/schema/tree.py (Node.centroids: list[list[float]] | None alongside existing embedding)
src/tool_index/clustering/upward.py (compute multi-centroids when reusing soft_cluster output)
src/tool_index/retrieval/traverser.py (score with max over centroids when present, fallback to embedding)
design.backwards_compat: If node.centroids is None, traverser uses node.embedding as today — old snapshots keep working.

measurement.metric: recall@10 on the natural-language eval corpus, plus per-category miss-rate diagnostic
measurement.command: Rebuild stages 4 and freeze; uv run scripts/eval_real_cases.py --run raw-tools --k 10 --decompose
ablation: M centroids + beam=2 (does multi-vector let us shrink beam back?)
measurement.success_threshold: recall@10 >= 0.94 AND cat_391687b6 miss rate drops below 25% (currently 55%)

risks: Snapshot size grows ~M-fold for inner nodes — fine for 90 tools, watch at 10k.
Centroid quality depends on soft_cluster temperature schedule; may need tuning.
If multi-vector recovers recall at beam=2, that is the strongest result (latency win + recall win).
decision_rule: Promote if recall@10 >= 0.94 with the broad-category miss rate halved. Most aligned with the in-house HILL implementation already on disk.
